Card

One section of a view set apart by a border or a background shift, with an optional title, one quiet action and a body.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • Sparingly. Content sits on the page by default, under a heading. Reach for a card only when grouping helps: a set of facts with an action that applies to all of them, or a region that must read as separate from the content around it.
  • For one or two sections of a view that hold different things, each laid out by what it holds.
  • With the sunken variant for a quieter region inside a bordered layout, where a second border would be noise.

When not to use it

  • For each of several similar items. A list of similar items is a list, not a card grid: use the list or the data table. Three or more sibling cards with the same structure fail the identical-card-grid rule.
  • Inside another card. Use one card and separate what is inside it with a heading or a divider. A nested card fails the nested-cards rule.
  • As the frame of a whole view, or around every section of it. Use headings and spacing on the page.
  • For a request that waits for an answer. Use the approval.
  • For a message about the view. Use an alert.
  • For content that floats above the page. Only an overlay takes a shadow, and a card never does.

Variants

bordered
The default, with no modifier class. A 1px border on the raised surface.
sunken gw-card--sunken
A background shift with no border. Keep quiet, muted text out of it: the muted colour does not reach 4.5:1 on the sunken surface in the light theme.

Accessibility

  • Use a section with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-card__title when the card has a title, so it is a named region. Give each card on a view a different title. Use a div for a card with no title.
  • gw-card__title is a heading at the level the view's outline needs. It is drawn at the size of body text whatever its level.
  • The header holds at most one action, in gw-card__action: a small quiet button or a link with the same classes. It is never primary. When several cards carry the same words, add an aria-label that starts with those words and names the card.
  • The header is 44px tall, so the small button's padded pointer target stays inside it.
  • A card is not focusable and takes no press. To make something pressable, put a link or a button inside it.
  • The card needs no script.
